correctness.rationale: For every path order at least two, the strictly positive tent vector makes each normalized row inner product have squared magnitude one, except the even central comparison where it is zero. The Rayleigh principle gives a universal reciprocal-squared-norm bound. Explicit probabilities sum to one and satisfy the proposed Jacobi eigenvector equations. The exact ground-state quadratic form is a sum of nonnegative weighted squares, proving the exhibited eigenvalue is the minimum. The equality recurrence forces the unique even design or the complete odd segment. Direct summation gives the sixth-over-cubed-order sharp limit. A standalone exact-arithmetic check passed 495 order-and-parameter instances; independent symbolic/numerical checks passed 71. These finite tests do not replace the universal proof or certify an exact multi-step exponent.

value.rationale: The problem models sparse absolute plus relative measurements in chains. Instead of generic semidefinite optimization or heuristic row importance, it gives every globally best iid sampling probability in closed form at all chain lengths, with a surprising parity boundary: even designs must discard a central difference row while odd designs have an exact continuum, usually keeping every row. This is a genuine support-choice/identifiability insight and supplies a sharp rate proportional to the inverse cube of path order.
